Second run passed fmt, file budget and all four Clippy configurations, then stopped in the workspace matrix part on runledger-postgres workflow_results::workflow_handle_deadline_poll_observes_result_without_listener (Timeout; 500 ms deadline against Docker PostgreSQL, host load average about 60 from other sessions; passed 3/3 alone; runledger has no dependency on the changed crates). The remaining steps were then run in order with no source change in between and all passed: test_matrix workspace, no-default-features, doctests, consumers, runlimit, scripts; cargo doc -D warnings; check_http_smokes. So no single uninterrupted verify.sh run passed end to end. Live, against a private disposable PostgreSQL 18.7 container: runlimit-postgres tests/attempts.rs 18/18 (unchanged file) and tests/attempt_state.rs 3/3; batter-runlimit attempts_live 14/14 on the final run; batter grants_live quota_cases authentication_attempts_admit_settle_and_clean_up_under_one_selection and the fixed-window/GCRA case 2/2 under the restricted role. PostgreSQL 16 (CI's version) was not run. Limitation found: batter-runlimit attempts_live::verification_and_transaction_share_one_parent_deadline (100 ms total budget) is intermittent under that load on the unmodified baseline too: baseline 21/25, changed 19/25, alternating runs. Not committed; these issues stay claimed and open until the change is committed. The cross-backend script has 30 observed results and 13 clock advances.

fields.description: Two tests with sub-second budgets failed intermittently on a host at load average 45-60 (many concurrent PostgreSQL containers), unrelated to the change under test (observed 2026-11-26 while verifying batter-ctk7.6/.7/.8). (1) crates/batter-runlimit/tests/attempts_live.rs verification_and_transaction_share_one_parent_deadline: 100 ms total budget with a 40 ms verification sleep; expects Interrupted in the Completion phase. On unmodified HEAD 29ac92d5 it passed 21/25, alternating with a changed build that passed 19/25. (2) runledger/runledger-postgres/tests/workflow_results.rs workflow_handle_deadline_poll_observes_result_without_listener: 500 ms wait timeout; failed once with Timeout inside scripts/verify.sh's workspace part, passed 3/3 alone. Neither failure was investigated beyond reproduction. Decide whether the budgets should scale, or the assertions should accept the phase the deadline actually interrupted.

data.text: Review follow-up (2026-11-26). An external review of the uncommitted change (Codex, gpt-6.2-astra, medium reasoning) raised three P2 findings, all accepted and fixed. (1) runlimit-postgres/src/attempts/row.rs clamped stored instants before 1970 to the epoch, which moved an expired pre-epoch lease's backoff start and could disagree with the previous signed evaluator on a hand-edited row; instants now map exactly by shifting the epoch to the earliest BIGINT, so order and differences are preserved, the clamp is gone and the 'invalid attempt clock' refusal no longer exists. This supersedes the clamp decision and that detail string in the earlier comment. (2) AttemptLease's derived Debug printed the lease token; it is now a manual impl that omits it, with a doctest. (3) The backend obligations and example were on a private module and so absent from rustdoc; they are now on AttemptState, and 'storing the settled state is optional' is qualified to nondecreasing evaluation instants. Verification of the post-review tree: scripts/verify.sh passed end to end in one uninterrupted run (exit 0; Rust 1.100.0, macOS aarch64). Live on a fresh private PostgreSQL 18 container: runlimit-postgres tests/attempts.rs 18/18 and tests/attempt_state.rs 3/3, batter-runlimit attempts_live 14/14, batter grants_live authentication_attempts case 1/1. PostgreSQL 16 not run. Still uncommitted; issue stays claimed and open.

Bound the single check and validated batch to the shard guards acquired for them. The first independent re-review found the analogous fixed-window capacity-denial regression. Fixed-window batches now do bounded cleanup for the full topology and check quota and capacity together in caller order. Fallible GCRA evaluation still precedes every clock/prune mutation and preserves suffix error precedence. A counted fixed-window algorithm test covers both exits. Final release probe on macOS arm64, 4,096 keys, one full shard, 901 samples from the in-lock clock sample to return: median 125 ns for quota denial and 167 ns for capacity denial at index zero. Focused all-feature package tests passed (84 including doctests), as did focused Clippy. Full final-tree verification and re-review in progress.

data.reason: Resolved the original four findings and all three follow-up findings. Single and batch sessions retain their inputs and routing. Fixed-window batches stop at either quota or capacity denial after bounded cleanup. GCRA arithmetic still precedes cleanup and later overflow wins. The changelog scopes allocation evidence to the measured paths. Both algorithms now describe entry writes, and only consuming commit methods on preflighted owners can apply them. Batch denial dispatch is exhaustive. In an isolated source copy, rustc rejected a premature write (E0603) and check/topology substitution (two E0061 diagnostics). The third independent uncommitted-tree review returned no findings. Final bash scripts/verify.sh passed on macOS arm64 with pinned Rust 1.100.0, including all four Clippy configurations, all six matrix parts, rustdoc and all HTTP smoke profiles. Three Runledger phased-handler deadline assertions failed on the initial run, passed in isolation and passed in the final full run. The final release probe reproduced medians of 125 ns for quota denial and 167 ns for capacity denial across 901 samples each, timed from the in-lock clock to return for 4096 keys on one shard.

fields.title: Bind memory quota configuration to the shard owner at construction

data.text: Pushed 055d8d55 to PR #129. BoundedShards owns its construction configuration for both quota algorithms. A temporary crate compile check rejected foreign configurations for execute_check, execute_batch, stats and recover_poisoned (four E0061 diagnostics). Capacity routing and uneven poison recovery have regression coverage. An independent read-only review of this change found no issues. Full local verification is running.

Final verification for 055d8d55: RUST_TEST_THREADS=2 bash scripts/verify.sh passed on macOS arm64 with Rust 1.100.0, covering all six matrix parts, four Clippy configurations, rustdoc and HTTP smokes. Earlier local runs stopped in runledger-postgres workflow_handle_pre_deadline_poll_timeout_runs_final_probe and batter-core scheduling_tool_process_controls. Both passed in isolation and in the complete run. Hosted Rust verification, macOS subprocess harness, native Runlimit PostgreSQL, policy and verified-tree checks passed. The separate fixed-window large-batch lock-duration finding remains open on PR #129.

data.reason: PR #129 commit 055d8d55 binds construction limits to the shard owner for both memory stores. Compile checks rejected all four mismatched-config calls, the follow-up review was clean, and full local and hosted verification passed.

data.text: PR #129 fixed-window stress test on macOS arm64, Rust 1.100.0, used clean master 445a8aaa and head 055d8d55. Out-of-tree two-pass prototype requires the shared fail-closed remaining_quota arithmetic and lazy pending-insertion counts. The initial prototype panicked and partially charged an injected over-limit batch. With the corrections, 384,000 deterministic operations matched decisions and observer traces, 76,800 competing calls preserved exact accounting, and debug/release runlimit-memory suites passed. Eight contenders on 4,096 warmed keys achieved 8,618/4,854/9,468 batches per second for master/PR/corrected. All-allowed p99 was 1.78/3.28/2.04 ms. The corrected late-denial path allocated zero after the clock sample versus 576 KiB on the PR. Large synchronized expiry was still modestly slower than master. This is prototype evidence; the performance fix has not landed.

fields.title: Remove buffered fixed-window batch writes while retaining atomic quota and capacity preflight

data.text: Implementation pushed as 88edfc5c to PR #129. Fixed-window preflight checks each occupied or vacant key in input order, uses fail-closed quota arithmetic, and lazily counts projected insertions. A private preflighted owner retains the original locks and checks into commit. The map entry API lets commit reuse a vacant or expired slot. Release Runlimit tests pass, including denial with a corrupt late counter and no prefix charge. Seven compile diagnostics confirm premature commit, proof forgery, check substitution and four foreign configuration calls are rejected. Production trace probes match master across 384,000 fixed-window operations and a further 30,000 operations per algorithm. One hundred 8-thread rounds (76,800 calls) found exact accounting. Local full verification, hosted checks and PR-wide review in progress.
